newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK SAX INDEX CONTINUES SLIDE IN FLAT TRADING.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK SAX INDEX CONTINUES SLIDE IN FLAT TRADING.

text.p: The Slovak SAX index
continued to decline in slugish trading on the Bratislava Stock
Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, pulled down by losses to several
blue chips.
Steel producer VSZ closed unchanged at 560 crowns, but its
average price - used for calculating the index - eased by 2.2
percent, accounting for a large part of the index's loss of
1.32 points. The SAX closed at 179.14.
"VSZ's final price is not its real value, as somebody
appears to have been holding it artificially high," said Peter
Krutil of Creditanstalt.
Brokers noted there was little interest among both domestic
and foreign investors, adding they did not expect a reversal of
the long-term decline in near future.
They also said small volumes traded muddled real values of
the shares, as larger packages were still available only for
higher prices.
Investors appear still to be waiting for further decline to
buy even cheaper shares, brokers said.
Oil refiner Slovnaft lost three crowns to close at 735, but
traded only 22 shares on the BSE floor.
Overall volume fell to 410,031 shares, most of which came
in the form of direct trades, from 1,227,880 traded on
Wednesday, while the turnover rose to 449.88 million crowns,
from 429.59 million.
-- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-563-3687
